headline: Goals are destinations you choose—clarity about what you want enables movement toward it
universal_truth: You can't hit a target you haven't set; knowing what you want is the first step to getting it
fun_facts: People who write down goals are 42% more likely to achieve them
The brain's reticular activating system filters information to notice goal-relevant opportunities
Specific goals lead to 90% better performance than vague intentions
discussion_questions: What do you actually want—specifically, not vaguely?
How clear are your goals? Could you measure progress?
What would you do differently if you had crystal clarity about your destination?

hook.script: You can't Google directions without entering a destination. You can't reach a target you haven't set. Goals are chosen destinations—clarity about what you want. Without them, you're just wandering.

cliff.script: Many people have vague wishes but not real goals. What's the difference, and why does it matter?

options.text: Effective goals are specific and measurable—vague desires provide no direction; clear targets let you navigate, measure progress, and know when you've arrived
options.response: Yes. 'Get fit' is a wish. 'Run a 5K by June' is a goal. Specificity enables planning, measurement, and course-correction. Clarity creates possibility.

options.text: Goals are just things you want
options.response: Wants are the start, but goals require clarity, specificity, and commitment...

fact1.title: Specificity Enables
fact1.script: Vague goals get vague results. 'Do better' offers no direction. 'Increase sales by 10% this quarter' creates a path. Specificity transforms wishes into achievable targets.

fact2.title: Filtering Function
fact2.script: Clear goals activate your brain's filtering system. You start noticing relevant opportunities that were always there but invisible. Clarity changes what you see.

fact3.title: The Courage to Choose
fact3.script: Setting a goal means choosing—and not choosing everything else. This takes courage. But not choosing doesn't avoid choice; it just chooses by default. Decide deliberately.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You can't hit a target you haven't set. Knowing what you want is the first step to getting it. Choose your destination.

outro.script: That's Day 283. Tomorrow, we'll explore things you do without thinking—habits. Until then, get specific about what you actually want.

growTrack.title: Goal Clarity Exercise - What Do You Actually Want?
growTrack.learning_objective: Convert vague wishes into specific goals
growTrack.activity: Pick one thing you 'want.' Now make it specific: What exactly? By when? How will you measure it? How will you know you've arrived? Transform a wish into a goal you can actually pursue.
